title: Founding of Meycauayan
description: Franciscan friars Juan de Placencia and Diego de Oropesa established the settlement as part of the First Franciscan Mission to the Philippines. The first church, made of nipa and bamboo, was dedicated to St. Francis of Assisi, with the poblacion first located in Malhacan.

title: Bocaue Founded
description: The neighboring town of Bocaue was established, a few years after Meycauayan.

title: Town Center Moves to Lagolo
description: After an earthquake damaged Malhacan and the church later moved again due to frequent visits by Aetas, Fr. Pedro Bautista transferred the town to a bamboo-forested area ("makawayan"), which gave the town its name. A concrete church was built at this new site.

title: Bocaue Under Meycauayan's Jurisdiction
description: Bocaue fell under Meycauayan's political control as one of its dependent towns.

title: Polo Separates
description: Polo (now Valenzuela) came under Meycauayan's jurisdiction before being detached as an independent town in 1623.

title: Concrete Bridge Built
description: A concrete bridge was constructed, standing today as a historical landmark of the town.

title: Philippine Revolution
description: Meycauayan contributed to the fight for independence through local heroes such as Gen. Andres Pacheco, Col. Ciriaco Contreras, Guillermo Bosque, and Liberato Exaltacion, among many others.

title: Marilao Becomes Independent
description: Marilao was the last town to separate from Meycauayan's jurisdiction.

title: Great Fire
description: A major fire destroyed the entire Town Center in Poblacion, setting back the municipality's development for years.

title: Reconstruction
description: With help from the provincial and national governments, infrastructure was rebuilt and rehabilitated after the 1949 fire.

title: First Class Municipality
description: A stronger economic base earned Meycauayan First Class Municipality status.

title: Cityhood
description: On December 10, 2006, voters ratified Republic Act 9356, converting Meycauayan into a component city — the third city in Bulacan after San Jose del Monte and Malolos.
